ai_industry.content_original:
無料でローカルAIを簡単にオフライン利用できるオープンソースアプリ「Hob」、Windows・Mac・Linux対応でPCに適したAIモデルの自動選択・ファイル操作・外部アプリ連携が可能
自分のPCでAIを動かすには、PCの性能に合ったAIモデルを選んだり実行環境を構築したりする必要があり、AIとのチャットだけでなく手元のファイルを読み取らせたり加工したりするには追加の設定が必要になる場合もあります。こうした作業を自動化する無料のオープンソースアプリ「Hob」は、PCに適したAIモデルを選んで実行環境を構築し、文書や表計算ファイルの解析・編集・グラフ作成などをチャットから実行できるツールです。
Hob — An easier way to use AI on your own computer. · hob.chat
https://www.hob.chat/
FrigadeHQ/hob: An easier way to use AI on your own computer. A free, open-source alternative to Claude and ChatGPT that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux. Private, and works offline.
https://github.com/FrigadeHQ/hob
◆Hobの導入方法
今回はNVIDIAのGPUを搭載したWindows 11上にインストールします。公式ページの「Download for Windows」をクリックし「Hob-windows-x64.exe」を保存。
保存したファイルを実行すると自動的にインストールが行われます。
インストール後、PCの調査が行われメモリやGPUに合うAIモデルが表示されるので「ダウンロードして開始」をクリック。
モデルがダウンロードされるとチャット画面が開きます。
Hobは日本語を含む32言語に対応しており、チャットに日本語を入力すると日本語で応答します。
◆Hobでできること
・CSVからグラフや報告書を作成
Hobはファイルを渡して内容を質問するだけでなく、Pythonを使って集計やグラフ作成などの処理を実行できます。例えば売上データのCSVを添付し「月別売上を合計して棒グラフを作り、変化を日本語で説明して」と入力します。
スクリプトが作成され実行。
結果としてグラフや集計内容がチャット内に表示されます。
・PDFや画像から情報を読み取る
PDFや画像も読み取れるため、文書の要約やスクリーンショットに写った内容の確認に利用できます。例えばPDFを添付し「このPDFの特徴を日本語で3項目にまとめて」と入力。
結果は正しくPDFの内容がまとめられていました。
画像の解析には別途ダウンロードされる小型の「Qwen3-VL」という画像認識モデルを使用します。
・フォルダーをプロジェクトとして扱う
サイドメニューの「新規プロジェクト」をクリックし、プロジェクト作成フォームで「名前」にプロジェクト名、「フォルダ」にテスト用フォルダーを登録し、「プロジェクト作成」をクリックするとプロジェクトが作成され指定したフォルダーのファイルをまとめてAIに扱わせることができます。
・その他の機能
このほかWeb検索・ローカル音声入力・チャット履歴のMarkdown保存・スキルの保存・Pythonツールの追加・MCPによる外部サービス連携にも対応しています。
MCPはAIから外部のアプリやサービスの機能を呼び出すための共通規格で、連携先によっては認証や通信が必要です。
◆オフライン利用とデータの保護
モデルの取得を済ませた後はネット接続を切ってもチャットや保存済みファイルの処理を続けられますが、外部サービスとの接続や追加パッケージの取得には通信が必要となります。ローカルLLMを利用するためプライバシー情報は外部には送信さられず、さらに「設定」の「プライバシー」で「Web アクセス」をオフにするとWeb検索やコードからのインターネットアクセス自体も無効化できます。
◆Hobの評価
ソーシャル系ニュースサイトのHacker NewsではHobについて議論が行われており「ただ動いてくれるものがあるだけで使い始めるのがずっと簡単になります」という評価がある一方、「モデルがあまり賢くない」という意見や「インストールされた18GBのモデルを簡単にアンインストールする方法がない」という指摘も投稿されています。
◆まとめ
HobはPCの性能に適したAIモデルを自動選択して実行環境を構築することを重視しており、推論の深さや利用モデルの変更には対応していますが、Temperatureやコンテキスト長、GPUの使用量などを細かく調整する機能は用意されていません。ローカルAIの性能を細かく調整するよりも、手軽に導入してチャットやファイル操作などに利用したい人向けのアプリです。

ai_industry.title: BiteTheBytes releases World Creator 4 in early access
ai_industry.summary_original: Big update to the terrain generator adds node-based workflow, macOS support - and the ability to create entire planets. See what else is new.
ai_industry.content_original:
BiteTheBytes releases World Creator 4 in early access
Originally posted on 12 October, and updated for the early access release.
BiteTheBytes has released World Creator 4, the next major version of its GPU-based terrain-generation software for game development, motion graphics and VFX work, in early access.
The release introduces a new core architecture, enabling the software to scale from generating conventional terrain to complete planetary environments.
Other key changes include a node-based terrain authoring environment, a new game-style real-time render engine, batch processing, and a MCP server to connect to external AI tools.
World Creator 4 is also be the first version of the software to be available for platforms other than Windows: the initial release supports macOS, with Linux support to come.
A procedural GPU-based terrain generator used by leading games and VFX studios
World Creator enables artists to create terrain through a combination of procedural and manual workflows.
Artists can create terrain by sculpting the basic 3D forms, and generating linear land forms like mountain ranges, rivers and roads along vector paths.
The terrain can be modified using filters, including those mimicking the effects of erosion and sediment deposition, previewing the results using World Creator’s built-in ray tracing renderer.
Users can export terrain to DCC applications and game engines in 3D formats like OBJ, FBX and glTF, or as 2D texture maps, including height maps and flow maps, with support for 32-bit EXRs.
The software has been used by artists at games and VFX studios including Blizzard Entertainment, Crytek, Blur Studio and Cinesite.
Click the image above to see BiteTheBytes demo of World Creator 4 from a recent livestream.
World Creator 4: a major overhaul of the software
World Creator 4 is a change of version numbering for the software, BiteTheBytes having used year-based versioning for some time now, so it follows on from World Creator 2026.4.
But more than that, it’s a major update, both above and under the hood, changing World Creator’s core architecture, core workflows, and the scale of the environments it can create.
Now scales from terrestrial terrain to complete planets
The biggest change is one of scope: World Creator 4 scales from generating chunks of terrestrial terrain to complete planetary landscapes.
It is possible to export the height and distribution data in a format that can be mapped onto a sphere, making it possible to create entire CG planets.
The workflow is made possible by World Creator’s new core architecture, which is powered by BiteTheBytes’ Cloddy SDK.
In the 2000s, Cloddy was the firm’s original flagship product, used in non-entertainment applications like GPS navigation systems and helicopter training simulators.
BiteTheBytes has now updated the SDK for modern hardware, providing a “fully GPU-driven planetary terrain pipeline”, extending real-world data with procedural detail.
It’s designed to process very large data sets: the render above is based on a 9GB USGS DEM model of Mars, which BiteTheBytes says is navigable in real time inside World Creator.
The firm plans to support MapTiler streaming and “expanded heightmap, DEM, and planetary data workflows”.
Node-based editing, unrestricted terrain sculpting, and new procedural models
World Creator 4 also replaces the software’s old layer system with a new node editor, making it possible to generate terrain non-destructively by wiring together nodes.
The release also implements “direct heightfield sculpting without the old level step system”.
Other changes include new models for procedural erosion, water and sand deposition; new high-detail filters; new object distribution controls; and over 110 procedural noise types.
New game-style render supplements the existing path tracer
The update also introduces an additional polygon-based renderer, “bringing conventional real-time game rendering alongside path tracing”.
Both the new renderer and the existing path tracer support NVIDIA’s render upscaling and frame interpolation system DLSS 4.5.
Batch processing, new MCP server, and support for macOS and Linux
New pipeline features include a batch processing system, making it possible for studios to handle repetitive tasks more efficiently.
The release also feature an integrated MCP server, making it possible to control World Creator with external AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT.
And last, but not least, the formerly Windows-only software is finally coming to macOS and Linux: the initial early access release supports macOS, and Linux support is “coming soon”.
Simplified new pricing
BiteTheBytes has also simplified World Creator’s previously complex pricing structure.
Whereas there used to be four separate price tiers, there are now only two: one for individual artists earning under $200,000/year, and one for companies.
For individual artists, perpetual licenses cost $149, while subscriptions cost $99/year.
At the lower end of the earning scale, that leaves the price of perpetual licenses unchanged, but slightly raises rental costs; if you earn above $100,000/year, it’s a saving either way.
For studios, perpetual licenses cost $899, while subscriptions cost $539/seat/year.
Price, system requirements and release date
World Creator 4 is available in early access for Windows and macOS, with Linux due soon.
It’s still in active development, so if you buy it now, you also get World Creator 3, which is the version intended for use in production. You can find price details in the story above.
Bridge tools are available for Blender, Cinema 4D, Godot, Houdini, Unity and Unreal Engine.
Visit the World Creator product website
Read more about World Creator 4 on BiteTheBytes’ Discord server

As well as being able to comment on stories, followers of our social media accounts can see videos we don’t post on the site itself, including making-ofs for the latest VFX movies, animations, games cinematics and motion graphics projects.

ai_industry.content_original:
The New York Times and a group of other publications have filed lawsuits against the company that makes the Brave web browser over alleged unlawful scraping to train AI and also letting users bypass their paywalls, as reported by Reuters.
The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
Brave has allegedly provided ‘stolen copyrighted content’ to many AI companies.
According to a complaint filed by the New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel, Brave Software has monetized its index of scraped websites by, in part, providing AI companies with paid access to “real-time online content from the Brave Index.” The AI companies then use that index to train their models, access content to “respond to specific user queries,” or both. Brave has allegedly provided “stolen copyrighted content” to “many” AI companies including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere.
Brave also promotes “hundreds of top publishers” as being accessible through its “Paywall blocker” feature in its browser.
“Brave has never asked for the Publishers’ permission to access their websites, much less to copy the material and provide it to users or other AI companies,” the complaint says. “On the contrary, as noted above, Brave allows its users to bypass the Publishers’ paywalls without their consent, and has taken other steps that prevent the Publishers from blocking Brave’s access to the Publishers’ websites. Brave has never compensated the Publishers for the unlawful use, copying, and distribution of the Publishers’ copyrighted content.”
“While we believe in the ethical and responsible use and development of AI, Brave has flouted established copyright law and ignored repeated requests by The Times to stop its infringing conduct,” Graham James, an NYT spokesperson, says in a statement to The Verge. “We filed this lawsuit to hold Brave accountable for stealing our content to power its own products and to provide it to some of the most prominent and well resourced generative AI companies in the world.”
“AI giants are now desperate to avoid getting caught red-handed stealing news from publishers, so Brave Software is selling them a back door to the journalism they know they have no right to,” says Steven Lieberman, the attorney who filed the lawsuit on behalf of the other three publications. “Buying stolen goods secondhand doesn’t make them legitimate. Brave must be held responsible for laundering pirated reporting for the AI industry.”
Brave, Anthropic, Mistral, SpaceXSI, and Cohere didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. “The New York Times is overpaying its attorneys and underpaying its journalists. (Who could’ve easily identified the disinformation in this suit.)” says Jesse Dwyer, Perplexity’s chief communications officer.
Update, November 2nd: Clarified that one lawsuit was filed by New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel, not the companies that run them. Also added a statement from the attorney who filed the lawsuit on behalf of those publications.

ai_industry.title: Autodesk releases Flame 2027.2
ai_industry.summary_original: Compositing and effects software gets the option to import USD scenes, and a new AI model for generating normal maps from video.
ai_industry.content_original:
Autodesk releases Flame 2027.2
Originally posted on 21 April 2026. Scroll down for details of the Flame 2027.2 update.
Autodesk has begun its Flame 2027 release cycle, the latest annual series of updates to Flame, its compositing, finishing and effects software
Flame 2027 itself introduces a new annotations system, two new AI models for generating depth maps from footage, and support for OpenTimelineIO.
Flare and Flame Assist, the cut-down editions of Flame, have also been updated.
New Annotations system lets you mark up clips directly inside Flame
New features in Flame 2027 include the Annotations system, for adding notes on the changes required to a shot directly inside Flame, rather than on a dedicated shot review platform. 
Users can add text or drawn annotations – lines, arrows, circles, rectangles or freehand strokes – to clips in the Player or the viewports.
Markers and Segment Markers with annotations are indicated in the timeline, and the annotations themselves can be selected from the Timeline Ribbon.
New AI models generate depth maps from indoor and outdoor scenes
There are also new AI features, in the shape of two new machine learning models for generating depth maps from still images or clips: ML Depth Indoor and ML Depth Outdoor.
As the names suggest, they generate depth data for entire scenes, unlike the existing Face Analysis model, which is optimized for human faces.
The depth data can then be used to create mattes in the Selective object or standalone ML Depth nodes.
It is also possible to load custom depth AI models in ONNX format.
Autodesk Assistant provides AI-generated answers to natural language tech questions
Flame 2027 also integrates Autodesk Assistant, the technical help system rolled out in other recent Autodesk product updates like Maya 2027. 
It searches Autodesk’s documentation to provide answers to simple natural-language questions.
Workflow improvements: better preservation of metadata and custom tokens
Workflow improvements include better preservation of metadata.
The frame-based metadata of imported clips can now be edited via a new Metadata node, and written to the OpenEXR file header when exporting a file sequence or publishing content.
It is also now possible to create custom tokens, for adding readymade text strings to text fields that support them.
Other changes include the option to add Markers in the Effects environment.
Pipeline integration: OpenTimelineIO support
Flame also now supports OpenTimelineIO, the new open standard for editorial cut information.
OpenTimelineIO files can be opened in the Conform environment, in the same way as AAF, XML or EDL files.
However, the current implementation only supports “basic OTIO sequences” and not the effects and effect properties from other VFX software that supports OpenTimelineIO.
In addition, Burn, Flame’s network rendering solution, is now supported on macOS, and there is a new command-line tool, flame_backup, for backing up and restoring projects.
Updated 27 July 2026: Autodesk has released Flame 2027.1.
New features include the Isolate tool, which replaces the existing GMask Tracer as the tool to use to create mattes using Selective Objects or machine learning models.
It is available both as a node, and via Timeline FX.
A new Pixel Expression node applies color-based changes to clips using the GLSL shading language. Unlike the existing Matchbox node, you don’t need to create a shader and a UI outside Flame: the shader code can be added directly to the UI.
Support for ProRes RAW in Media Import
The other major change is support for ProRes RAW clips in MediaHub, making it possible to import footage recorded on devices like the iPhone 17 Pro and Atomos recorders.
In addition, the machine learning upscale models have been replaced with new models that require less memory on Linux, making it possible to run them on higher-resolution clips.
Updated 7 November 2026: Autodesk has released Flame 2027.2.
It’s quite a significant update, with new features including a new machine learning model for generating normal maps from video, for use in relighting or applying effects to a shot.
Flame already had an AI normal map generator, but it was specifically for human faces.
The new model is available as a Matchbox shader, in the Selective object, and in the Normal Map object.
Action now imports USD scenes, as well as Alembic and FBX files
Users can also now import USD scenes into Action, Flame’s 3D compositing environment.
The change should help Flame play nicer in visual effects pipelines, many of which are now based around USD.
The implementation supports USD geometry, materials, lights and cameras, and all of the USD file extensions, including USDZ files (.usd, .usda, .usdc and .usdz).
Other new features and workflow improvements
Other changes to Action include a new 3D Primitive node for adding geometric primitives to a scene, and support for all of the OpenSubdiv schemes for subdividing geometry.
Pipeline integration changes include the option to use Python Hooks to control Batch setups, and to publish sequences in OpenTimelineIO format.
There are also a number of workflow improvements and changes to supported media formats.
Pricing and availability
Flame 2027, Flame Assist 2027 and Flare 2027 are compatible with Rocky Linux 8.10/9.5/9.7 and macOS 14.0+. The software is available rental-only. 
Flame subscriptions cost $650/month or $5,215/year. Flame Assist and Flare subscriptions cost $2,775/year.
The Autodesk website also still offers $5,215/year subscriptions to Lustre, the Flame product family’s color grading software, although it has not been updated since 2024.
Read a full list of new features in the Flame 2027 releases in the online documentation

As well as being able to comment on stories, followers of our social media accounts can see videos we don’t post on the site itself, including making-ofs for the latest VFX movies, animations, games cinematics and motion graphics projects.

ai_industry.title: Disneyland Is Training a Class of AI Robot Interns
ai_industry.summary_original: From Pixar robots to help you park your car to droids roaming Star Wars land, physical AI is popping up all over Disneyland.
ai_industry.content_original:
If you’ve ever driven to Disneyland, you know that parking is a challenge. When the parks open each morning, long lines clog the nearby streets as engines idle, families waiting anxiously to enter the parking structure so they can start their day at the parks.
Parking attendants can only do so much to handle the tens of thousands of cars arriving every day at the Disneyland Resort. But what if a cutesy autonomous robot from Pixar’s Cars series could help direct traffic flow and guide you right into your parking spot?
That’s a project being tested with FieldAI, a company that builds the AI brains for robots. In a demo video at the Disney Accelerator Demo Day on Tuesday, Disney and FieldAI showed footage of robots that would assist with guiding cars through the parking process.
More from CNET
“Imagine if a character from Cars or robots from Wall-E direct you where to park when you arrive,” Gary Daniels, senior vice president of products and experiences at Disney Experiences Technology, said. “The work we are doing now is a great way to see how the robots function, and, as important, how people respond.”
Other companies build the robots; FieldAI slaps its physical AI solution in a box on top of them, having worked so far with around 30 different robot types, shapes and sizes. The box is equipped with multiple cameras that serve as the robot’s “eyes and ears,” helping the AI model process what it’s experiencing in real time. The robots also collect data while operating.
During the event at Walt Disney Studios, FieldAI showcased a Boston Dynamics robot dog and a miniature version of the BBX droids from The Mandalorian and Grogu that roam Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge at Disneyland. FieldAI-enabled robots have already been deployed in Disneyland at Galaxy’s Edge on the BBX droids, though they hedged that this is in its early stages.
“Our intelligence is on the bigger version and operating in the park already,” FieldAI CEO Ali Agha told reporters.
David Min, vice president of Disney Innovation, told me it could also be used on characters that interact with guests at parks, naming Olaf and The Hulk as examples.
Another project with Disney involves getting multiple robots to talk to each other to coordinate missions.
Headquartered in Irvine, California, with offices in the San Francisco Bay Area, Boston and Pittsburgh, FieldAI primarily works in construction environments and energy facilities to complete tasks like inspections, material transport and supporting construction. But this is easily translated to a theme park environment, where paths and crowds are constantly changing, and autonomous robots need to account for that without needing mapping or GPS.
“Our BBX proof of concept explores how to bring that navigation together with Disney character performance,” said Doug Fidaleo, lab director, Disney Research, Walt Disney Imagineering R&D. “That’s what drew us to FieldAI: deep experience deploying robots in demanding, unstructured environments with uneven terrain, changing layouts and unexpected obstacles.”
Some of the use cases Agha gives include robots supporting security, perimeter patrols, helping cast members backstage and enabling more in-park experiences — even delivering items to people waiting in line for a ride.
“This is a highly self-autonomous system that operates without a positioning system,” Agha said.
A robot internship at Disneyland
Physical Intelligence (Pi) is another company that builds AI brains for robots. Also showcased during Disney’s Accelerator Demo Day, Pi is focused less on roaming droids that can help or entertain guests and instead on robots helping Disney cast members with backstage tasks.
Namely: picking up, folding, cleaning and sorting the 3D glasses used for rides like Toy Story Midway Mania and shows like Mickey’s PhilharMagic.
It’s an unpleasant task that’s a major pain point for cast members who have to spend a long time in a small room completing it several times a day. It also requires “dexterous manipulation,” with Pi previously working on general-purpose robots that perform tasks like folding and stacking, using robots that have grippers rather than five-digit hands.
Sourish Jasti, a technical staffer with Pi, said the company recently spent 12 days at Disneyland between midnight and 6 a.m. collecting data, testing logistics and moving its robots in and out of the park to see whether it could help with sorting the 3D glasses.
“This was like a robot internship,” Jasti said, adding that physical AI is like a toddler, in that it learns from actually doing things.
The robots — which, much like FieldAI, Pi doesn’t build but instead installs the brains for — could be either a humanoid on wheels or just a mechanical arm. There are cameras on the base and cameras on the wrists to help the AI model “see” what it’s doing as it picks up and sorts the glasses.
“We intend to have robots interning in many different spaces with Disney,” Jasti said, pointing to not only the theme parks but also Disney’s studios, hotel rooms and cruise liners, which he calls “mini cities.”
For both Pi and FieldAI, Min said the benefit is that using AI can train the robots much faster to do the tasks Disney needs them to do — and that going to companies like these, which are already well-established in fields like construction and manufacturing, makes it easier to transfer those skills to the theme parks.
Whether they’re roaming around parking structures or lands, or backstage helping workers, the AI-equipped autonomous robots are solving problems for Disney.
“The connection is through the core capabilities that we’re developing for our robots,” Fidaleo said. “Robots that can perceive the world around them, can act in the physical world and adapt when things change.”
Disney is continuing to push technology from the audio-animatronic figures used on rides like Pirates of the Caribbean, making them more sophisticated to build an immersive experience.
“From the expressive Na’vi shaman to a robotic Spider-Man flying through the air, to a walking baby Groot, each advance changes how we can experience a character in the physical world,” Fidaleo said. “The park of the future will be teeming with robot characters.”

ai_industry.title: Affinity’s creative studio is now available on iPad for free
ai_industry.summary_original: Canva is giving digital creatives a new way to design, illustrate, and edit photos on their iPads, and it doesn't have to cost them a thing. After relaunching the Affinity creative suite as an all-in-one desktop app last year, Canva has now introduced Affinit…
ai_industry.content_original:
Canva is giving digital creatives a new way to design, illustrate, and edit photos on their iPads, and it doesn’t have to cost them a thing. After relaunching the Affinity creative suite as an all-in-one desktop app last year, Canva has now introduced Affinity for iPad, which provides the same pro-grade tools for vector graphics, photo editing, illustration, and page layouts in a format optimized for Apple Pencil and touchscreens.
Affinity’s creative studio is now available on iPad for free
Affinity for iPad has a new Sketch Studio that’s designed for freehand drawing and simplifying sketch-to-vector workflows, including optimized tools for masking and automatically converting rough sketches into cleaner geometric shapes. The app also supports Apple Pencil Pro capabilities like natural gestures, pressure sensitivity, tilt, barrel roll, squeeze, and hover, allowing creatives more control over tools and shortcuts.
“Affinity for iPad delivers the full power of Affinity, together with the versatility and portability of iPad,” Affinity product design head Neil Ladkin said in the announcement. “Every development decision was made by people who create on iPad themselves, from how the Apple Pencil responds to where the tools sit. If you’re the sort of person who rotates the canvas 40 times to get one line right, Affinity for iPad was made by people who’ve done exactly that.”
Sketch, vector design, photo editing, and layout projects can all be saved to the same .af file to limit tasks needing to be exported, converted, or remade, but Affinity for iPad is also compatible with all major design file types. Canva has added its AI Studio to the app, which includes features like Generative Expand for extending backgrounds, automatic motion blur and noise reduction, and image resolution scaling.
When Canva acquired Affinity-developer Serif in 2024, some users were concerned that Affinity would move from a one-time license to a subscription model and adopt Canva’s generative AI tech, eradicating a large part of the creative suite’s appeal compared to rival design software provider Adobe. Canva and Serif pledged not to force users into subscribing to the service, and so far that’s still the case.
Affinity for iPad’s core sketch, vector, photo editing, and layout tools are completely free for individuals, though they require a free Canva account. The suite of AI tools is optional and requires a Canva Pro subscription to access, which starts at $18 per month.

ai_industry.title: Don’t be fooled by the fake hair on these famous baldies
ai_industry.summary_original: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They're both famously bald, and that definitely hasn't changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X, Threads, and Blues…
ai_industry.content_original:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They’re both famously bald, and that definitely hasn’t changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X, Threads, and Bluesky in which they both have substantially more hair than their usual shaved look, which in Bezos’ case appears to be very freshly transplanted. It’s all just photo editing fakery, AI or otherwise.
Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
In the era of easy AI fakery, edited paparazzi photos are a reminder that not everything is what it seems.
It’s unclear how viral these posts are, but they’re prevalent enough that a few members of the Verge team have encountered them in their social media feeds. Some people who shared them claimed (or were seemingly fooled into believing) that Bezos and Statham had undergone hair transplant surgery. Generative AI tools have made this kind of photo manipulation or outright creation more accessible and convincing, and because AI labeling solutions on social media broadly suck at flagging this fakery, it’s easy to be misled unless you’re wary of everything you see online. In a world where social media shitposters can turn engagement into a revenue stream, they’re not going to stop churning out attention-grabbing fabricated nonsense anytime soon.
We don’t know if AI tools were used to make the follicled Bezos and Statham edits — none of the images I tested flagged for Content Credentials or SynthID markers. We also can’t fully establish when they were first posted or who made them, but they are definitely fake, and it only took me a couple of minutes to confirm it.
In both cases, I ran the photos through Google’s reverse image search tool. For the Bezos debunk, I found photographs of him in a similar background environment and wearing the exact same outfit (with, yes, no hair) that included a watermarked image credit at the bottom left. Searching for the credit then led me to the original photographs in their unaltered state, which were taken in 2023. Finding the original tressless images of Statham was even easier — the reverse image search immediately surfaced watermarked versions of the originals, which were snapped by a paparazzo in 2011.
There’s other evidence too if you know what to look for. The main flag is that it’s probably impossible for Bezos and Statham to be realistic candidates for hair replacement surgery anyway; it requires you to have enough “donor” hair to sacrifice from the back and sides of your head to then replant closer to your desired hairline. You can technically take it from other places (or even other people), but doing so is incredibly rare due to undesirable results and rejection concerns. Transplant patients also typically experience some pretty dramatic facial swelling for the first week or so, which Bezos shows no signs of. Wigs, toupees, and other hair systems can also be used as nonpermanent hair restoration solutions, but as someone who used to make and install them professionally, it would be an astounding whoopsie for someone as rich and connected as Bezos to go this route and still end up looking like a Chia Pet.
This isn’t the first time photo-manipulated fakery has fooled people across social media, and with ongoing generative AI advancements, it probably won’t be the last. Previous incidents gave us the viral swagged-out pope, and recent trends have seen paparazzi photographs of celebrities like Callum Turner, Harry Styles, and Noah Schnapp being manipulated to remove their shirts. These kinds of edits are typically designed to rack up likes, reposts, and other engagement — they play into our fascination with celebrities’ lives with fabricated situations that are just outlandish enough to be believable, grab our attention, and be shared around as the latest hot gossip by those who are fooled, or who simply don’t care to verify the facts.
If you’re ever unsure if there’s fakery afoot with images of famous faces, just remember that most of the convincing edits (AI or otherwise) are based on real photos that you can hunt down to verify the original source.

ai_industry.title: Rockstar Will Be Keen to Release GTA 6 on PC Sooner Rather Than Later Because of AI Clones, Former Dev Says
ai_industry.summary_original: Rockstar may officially release GTA 6 on PC soon after console over concern about AI-generated clones, one former developer has said.
ai_industry.content_original:
Rockstar may officially release GTA 6 on PC soon after console over concern about AI-generated clones, one former developer has said.
In an interview with IGN sister site RPS, former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible, due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.
People are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable on X/Twitter to modders shoving Minecraft and Elden Ring together. Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline.
Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones, but concern that GTA 6 could pop up on PC soon after it hits PlayStation and Xbox remains.
There is also concern around the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware ahead of the release of GTA 6. This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.
"[Generative AI] really has changed the world," Vermeij said, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking.
"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest. I don't see it. But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job.
“But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years how that's going to pan out."
In October, GamesBeat reported that Rockstar was indeed planning to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two did not comment on the report.
If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.
The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.
Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”
Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.
We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park, how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme, and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely.
Analysts expect GTA 6 will make over $5 billion in launch week alone. GTA 6 is scheduled to be released on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

ai_industry.title: A new way of measuring AI models suggests China's threat to OpenAI and Anthropic may have been overblown
ai_industry.summary_original: Chinese AI models fell behind US rivals after Artificial Analysis revamped its tests, raising questions about open-weight AI's performance.
ai_industry.content_original:
Chinese AI models have fallen sharply behind American rivals in a closely watched ranking, raising fresh questions about whether the threat from cheaper, freely available AI technology has been exaggerated.
Artificial Analysis, a prominent independent firm that measures AI performance, recently overhauled its testing system to better reflect how people actually use the technology.
One crucial change: Many of the tests are now kept secret, making it harder for AI companies to train their models specifically to perform well on them.
The results were striking.
Artificial Analysis said the best so-called open-weight AI models had trailed the overall leader by just three points under the previous system. Under the new system, that gap widened to 12 points.
The 12-point gap included Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro. Among models with publicly released weights, the leaders scored just 32 points, compared with 58 for the then overall leader, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5.
The findings could have major implications for the AI industry and the billions of dollars investors are pouring into it.
Chinese companies have been releasing powerful AI models that other businesses can download and adapt, often at lower costs than American alternatives. This fueled concern that companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic could struggle to charge premium prices for their proprietary technology.
The new rankings suggest that threat may have been overstated, potentially strengthening the investment case for Anthropic's planned IPO and a possible future OpenAI listing.
Sridhar Ramaswamy, CEO of Snowflake and a former Google executive, highlighted the significance of the testing change.
"The day benchmarks went private, the open-model gap went from 3 points to 12," he wrote on X. "Were open models catching up, or was the test leaking?"
"Benchmark hacking"
His point: When AI companies know exactly how their technology will be tested, they can train it to excel at those particular tasks. That doesn't necessarily mean their models perform equally well in the real world.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other AI experts have called this "benchmark hacking." Keeping the tests secret makes these hacks harder.
The new results suggest American companies have a bigger lead than previously believed, particularly in complex scientific tasks. Even Claude Haiku 5.5, a smaller Anthropic model, outperformed every AI model with publicly released weights.
Even proponents of open-weight models admitted something has likely been awry.
"I do think the previous index was flattering the open weight models too strongly," said Nathan Lambert, cofounder of Trillium Labs, which researches large language models, especially open-weight models.
Smaller usage
There's another reason to question the threat from open-weight AI models: How much are people actually using them?
Dax Raad, cofounder of software development company OpenCode, recently examined traffic through OpenRouter, a popular service that lets developers access AI models from different providers.
He estimated that almost all the previous day's DeepSeek traffic flowing through OpenRouter could be handled by a single rack of powerful Nvidia computers, costing roughly $6 million to $7 million.
That's a surprisingly small amount of computing power given the enormous attention Chinese AI models have attracted.
OpenRouter represents only a slice of the market, so its figures don't capture all demand for open-weight models.
But Raad's broader point is important: Much of the industry's enormous AI infrastructure investment is being driven by major providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, rather than the smaller developers using open models.
Consider the more than 1 billion people who use ChatGPT every month. These folks are using OpenAI's closed AI models all the time — potentially way more activity than is captured by AI gateway services such as OpenRouter.
Two questions
Together, the rankings and usage figures raise two questions about open-weight AI: Is it really as good as the leading American technology, and is demand as substantial as the hype suggests?
There are important caveats.
Trillium's Lambert said open-weight models remain highly competitive in areas such as software development, and can offer businesses greater control and potentially lower costs.
Still, the new evidence challenges a powerful narrative that has shaped the industry: that Chinese AI companies are rapidly catching America's leaders and threatening their business models.
For investors weighing the enormous valuations of OpenAI and Anthropic, that distinction matters enormously.

ai_industry.title: Anthropic Addresses Video Game Cloning With Minor Claude Update
ai_industry.summary_original: There’s a fine line between AI creations inspired by video games and those that are infringing copyright.
ai_industry.content_original:
One of AI’s biggest selling points is its ability to build things quickly. AI models can help users sort through mountains of files, generate videos that have Hollywood studios worried, and create everything from websites and businesses to custom video games. With what’s called vibe coding, ordinary people can build playable video games in minutes using simple text prompts in popular AI tools like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini.
But the AI company Anthropic appears to be drawing a line in the sand about what kinds of games its AI model Claude can make. If a Claude user is trying to recreate someone else’s intellectual property, the AI tool will decline to build it.
That’s according to Addy Osmani, an engineering leader at Anthropic who posted on X. He was responding to concerns that Anthropic had changed Claude Opus 5.5 to prevent it from generating copies of existing games, which could violate copyright rules and the company’s usage policy.
More from CNET
“Original games, genre games, and games built from your own designs and assets are meant to keep working,” Osmani said. “We’ll continue to iterate to ensure we’re striking the right balance.”
He offered to review cases where amateur game developers believe Claude wrongly refused their requests.
A representative for Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Homage versus infringement
Anthropic’s stance, as expressed by Osmani, acknowledges that using AI to try to clone a video game, even a simple one, could constitute intellectual property infringement, an issue that predates the rise of AI tools like Claude.
Even with the change, Claude will still generate video games that resemble popular hits from the past few decades. A CNET request to build a game “that resembled Breakout but with the word Claude on each brick” yielded a playable web version of the arcade classic, but not one that any video game fan would mistake for the original.
The same thing happened after Flappy Bird became a hit in 2014, spawning a wave of copycat games in app stores. Copyright infringement of games is complicated, said David Kocan, an intellectual property lawyer at Nixon Peabody who co-leads the firm’s esports and gaming team.
“This is something courts have wrestled with long before AI came along,” Kocan said. “The basic distinction has always been that copyright protects a game’s original creative expression, but generally not its underlying ideas, rules, or gameplay mechanics. Copyright protects the game you created, not the genre you helped popularize.”
You can’t copyright the concept of, say, a battle royal game or a side-scrolling platformer, which is why when a new type of game emerges as a hit, you’ll see many similar games.
“That distinction may sound straightforward in theory, but in practice, the line between borrowing an idea and copying someone’s creative expression can be blurry,” Kocan said. “That’s particularly true in gaming, where so much of the experience combines functional mechanics with creative expression.”
RTB Ruhan, founder and CEO of Null Station, an animation and video game art studio, said that AI has made it”fast and cheap” to cross the line into infringement, allowing people with no art or design skills to clone a popular game. But that doesn’t mean someone can publish or sell a cloned game without running into trouble.
“‘(Claiming) AI made it’ won’t protect them,” Ruhan said.
His studio uses a simple test.
“Remove the title and logo and ask whether a player could still tell the two games apart,” Ruhan said. “If they can’t, you’ve crossed the line.”
Are AI companies responsible for game clones?
Legal experts CNET spoke with said there are no laws requiring AI companies to outlaw game clones on their tools. But adding those guardrails could prevent trouble down the road, said Eric Blatt, a corporate, securities and intellectual property lawyer at Scale and a former examiner at the US Patent and Trademark Office.
“Anthropic is prudent to tap the brakes here,” Blatt said. “If Claude — Anthropic-owned software operating on Anthropic servers — receives an instruction to copy a game, and if Claude then copies the game, there is a facially plausible argument that Anthropic performed the copying. The chat logs would be a gold mine for the plaintiff’s counsel.”
Blatt said that litigation hasn’t kept pace with AI’s growth, but he thinks lawsuits could quickly follow if a rebuilt game made with AI directly threatens a company’s business model.
But some of those attempts could be stopped before they start if AI models refuse to make exact copies.
“Ultimately, copyright law draws the legal boundaries,” Kocan said. “But AI companies have to decide where they’re comfortable drawing their own. And those aren’t necessarily going to be the same thing.”
